# Environment variables — `incident-responder`

<!-- generated by platform/scripts/gen_env_doc.py from distribution.yaml; do not edit by hand -->

`incident-responder` reads the following variables from its profile `.env` (generated as `.env.EXAMPLE` on install). All are credentials or endpoints — they are **never committed and never logged**. Set them in `.env`, then forward the names into the Kali sandbox via `docker_forward_env` in `config.yaml`.

## Reference

| Variable | Required | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WAZUH_API_URL` | no | — | Wazuh Server API base URL, e.g. https://wazuh.internal:55000 (read-only) |
| `WAZUH_API_USER` | no | — | Read-only Wazuh Server API user (RBAC: *:read only) |
| `WAZUH_API_PASSWORD` | no | — | Password for the read-only Wazuh Server API user |
| `WAZUH_INDEXER_URL` | no | — | Wazuh Indexer (OpenSearch) URL for cross-host alert correlation, e.g. https://wazuh.internal:9200 |
| `VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY` | no | — | Optional VirusTotal API key for hash/IOC enrichment (metadata lookups only; no file uploads) |
| `MISP_URL` | no | — | Optional MISP threat-intel platform base URL, e.g. https://misp.internal (read-only) |
| `MISP_API_KEY` | no | — | Optional MISP automation key (read-only role) for IOC enrichment/correlation |

## `.env` template

Copy into the profile's `.env` and fill real values (do not commit it):

```dotenv
# Wazuh (SIEM) — Server API + Indexer
WAZUH_API_URL=   # optional
WAZUH_API_USER=   # optional
WAZUH_API_PASSWORD=   # optional
WAZUH_INDEXER_URL=   # optional

# Other
VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY=   # optional
MISP_URL=   # optional
MISP_API_KEY=   # optional
```

## Forward into the sandbox

Add the names (not values) to `config.yaml` so the Kali container sees them:

```yaml
terminal:
  docker_forward_env:
    - WAZUH_API_URL
    - WAZUH_API_USER
    - WAZUH_API_PASSWORD
    - WAZUH_INDEXER_URL
    - VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY
    - MISP_URL
    - MISP_API_KEY
```

## Handling rules

- Credentials come **only** from these env vars — never hard-coded, printed, or committed (platform Security Policy).
- Prefer **read-only / least-privilege** credentials for every integration; forward names into the sandbox via `docker_forward_env`.
- Optional vars left unset simply disable or degrade the feature that needs them.
- Rotate any credential that may have been exposed; `.env` is in `.gitignore` and must stay untracked.
